Senior Vice President of Operations

Some Self customers are establishing credit for the first time. Others are rebuilding it. "Life happens - kids, divorce, unexpected bills, loss of jobs or family members. It happens." says Elizabeth O'Connor, Senior Vice President of Operations at Self Financial. "There's all different reasons why credit can be bad."
Protecting the moments of truth

Elizabeth interviewed "10 different AI companies, if not more" before she chose Lorikeet. She had run process, technology and automation work in contact centers for more than twenty years, but had never implemented AI. Three criteria decided it.
Self took its first live calls on Lorikeet in April 2026 as limited tests. The Lorikeet team was on site with Self, and the rollout moved in careful steps.

Part of that trust came from the speed of the work. "We would get feedback and literally on the call, make the change, and the change was there," she says. On April 20, 2026, Self moved all voice traffic to Lorikeet, 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
Solving problems end to end, at any hour

When a builder calls Self today, Lorikeet's voice agent answers and has a conversation with them. It works out what they need, then takes the action. It can send a replacement card, unlock a card, activate a new one, start fraud handling, and identify the transaction behind a dispute. Each action reads from and writes to Salesforce, Self's system of record, through Self's own API layer.
"We weren't just able to answer more contacts 24/7, we were actually able to solve problems with that that we were not able to solve before," Elizabeth says.

The weekend service also changed Mondays. "We've seen a significant swing in how our Mondays occur because of the servicing that we're able to get over the weekend with Lorikeet voice. We have seen a similar reduction in early morning traffic thanks to Lorikeet’s 24/7 voice service versus the 7-7 we had previously " Elizabeth says.

With routine requests resolved by the agent, Self's human team works on the moments of truth. "Because Lorikeet can handle some of the easier to middle difficult conversations, our agents have more time to solve the problem," Elizabeth says. "Anything that's coming to you at this point now are going to be difficult challenges, and we want you to take the time to solve that."

Elizabeth plans for the load that comes with it. Back-to-back complex contacts wear people down, so Self gives agents more time on each problem and more space between problems. "The burnout leads to attrition, and attrition leads to all other types of problems," she says.
Her second lesson is about preparation. "You're only as good as the FAQs or policies and procedures you come to the table with," she says.

She has also set her team a harder challenge: a request that today waits in a work queue. "I've given them a really cool test case that I think could take us from an end to end processing that gives a customer who might wait ten to fifteen days for resolution on something immediate resolution," she says. "It's the first use case, and I have so many more on the list."

Taptap Send is one of the largest cross-border payments platforms in the world, processing billions of dollars each year for millions of customers. Built AI-native from the ground up, it is engineered for speed, low cost and reliability, delivering money across more than 35 send markets and over 80 receive markets spanning Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa.

Taptap Send evaluated multiple AI customer service providers before choosing Lorikeet. The deployment runs on European-hosted infrastructure integrated with Taptap Send’s systems, with real-time customer data access across email, voice and chat.

The ease of set-up and optimisation using Lorikeet’s Coach stood out for Taptap Send. Rather than configuring endless workflows by hand, the team states its goals, gets recommendations and has Coach take action. That has sharpened their view of current performance and made it far easier to improve.
